cultural.vision_reason: This is a classic strip-woven kente-style wrapper cloth with narrow warp-faced strips, supplementary weft geometric and figurative motifs, and banded borders — a technique and style strongly associated with Ewe (and Asante) weavers in Ghana.

physical.title: garment; cloth
physical.summary:
Wrapper; hand-woven plain weave cotton cloth with supplementary weft in rayon thread. Composed of 21 narrow warp-faced strips machine-sewn together at the selvedges. Two alternating strips: blue and white cotton warp with black cotton and gold rayon weft; banded border at each end with continuous supplementary weft patterns in blue and gold rayon. Red cotton warp and weft; banded border at each end with supplementary weft in gold rayon. Unworked warp fringe on all strips.

Main design elements worked in discontinuous supplementary weft in multi-coloured rayon thread. Designs include: diamond, chameleon, bird, sword, key, quadruped, butterfly. These mainly representational motifs are set within a larger diamond formed from 24 rectangles arranged in stepped pattern across the strips. Rectangles are worked in discontinuous supplementary weft: blue and gold rayon on the red strips; burgundy and gold rayon on the blue and white strips.
